newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia 1996 cut diamond output seen flat - official.
newsitem.headline: Russia 1996 cut diamond output seen flat - official.

text.p: Russian production of cut diamonds this year will be flat on 1995's level, a prominent industry official said on Thursday.

Yevgeny Bychkov, former head of the disbanded State Committee for Precious Metals and Stones and now president of the private Russian Diamonds Cutters' Association, told Interfax news agency that domestic cutters needed about $1.2 billion worth of rough stones a year.

He said Almazy Rossii-Sakha, Russia's main diamond producer and sole authorised exporter which is in talks with South African De Beers, was selling stones to domestic cutters at prices 7-15 percent above world market levels.
The report valued Russia's 1995 cut diamond production as worth $1.0 billion.
ARS and De Beers have not yet finalised an agreement under which Russia will export diamonds abroad.
Bychkov said the agreement could create a shortage of raw materials for the domestic cutting industry, which he is seeking to bolster.

He said domestic cutters needed about $1.2 billion worth of rough stones a year, while ARS planned to sell not less than $550 million worth of stones to De Beers. ARS plans to produce about $1.35 billion worth of rough diamonds this year.
